title: "Reality Testing"
subtitle: Scenes from an Imagined TV Pilot
text:
Yes, I usually write articles about health. Sometimes I write silly articles. Sometimes I write poetry! But other times, like today, I write silly scenes from TV pilots that I’m never going to do anything with. Given I generally reserve weekends for absurd material in the newsletter, today I welcome you to the first few scenes of my completely fictional TV pilot. None of what you will read is inspired by real life. None of it totally happened in the way you will read. It is a work of fiction, and fancy, and I am very creative, thank you in advance. Some stories are inspired by real events—this is not one of them.

Subscribe now

“Reality Testing” is set at the beginning of the pandemic, in an ambitious medical start-up that’s trying to change the world of healthcare. It’s a clinic, called Brooklyn Brains. It thinks it will be a start-up. There are a few things they don’t know yet, and those issues might doom them.

The Cast of Main Characters:

Allegra Perillo, RN: Allegra is our hero, every woman, through his eyes, we see the story. She is a nurse, and a good one, but can’t help notice absurdity and wonder what to do.

Owen Moore, MD: Owen is a psychiatrist, he works with children and adults, and he’s also kind of a freakish, savant genius, which doesn’t always help him. He’s bumbling, awkward, slightly, overweight, and funny. If Seth Rogen and Isaac Newton had a child: it might be this guy. He hates writing notes and loves artificial intelligence.

Calvin McBeattie: Calvin is a deeply strange man. He imagines himself to be an entrepreneur but has never succeeded at that. He’s got one friend, JT. He thinks he’s found a winner in “Brooklyn Brains.” He’s got a thick Irish accent and is often high on mushrooms.

Carly MacDuff, MD: Owen’s wife, and business partner. No nonsense, exasperated, and frequently forced to raise an eyebrow. A burning house would barely make her blink.

JT Rand: the Founder Of MendMind, a psychedelic platform solution as a service, and formerly worked for an Ill-fated Ride Share Platform, called “Syft”—it was an arbitrage play that called either Lyft or Uber based on which would be cheaper. He’s somehow Calvin’s business partner.

Kevin: A trainee therapist who comes from a wealthy family.

The date?

One week before the Covid pandemic is announced to the world. The opening scene takes place in a haphazard office, in a converted recording studio, and in Williamsburg Brooklyn.

ACT I:

Allegra: So, did you hear about this Covid thing?

Owen: You’re referring to the novel coronavirus that was identified in Wuhan China?

Allegra: No one’s ever gonna call that.

Owen: Well, I mean people like things that are novel, right?

Allegra: No. Nobody says that.

Owen: So, this is gonna be a branding problem, isn’t it?

Allegra: Did you have “doctor things” to be doing?

[beat]

Owen: I did them already.

Allegra: Including your notes?

Owen: Well, maybe I didn’t finish all my notes.

Allegra: You’d rather be talking about the hero’s journey for a novel coronavirus from Wuhan, China— instead of getting your work done?

Owen: That work would involve… typing.

Allegra: Oh my God, are you going to keep going on about how AI needs to do your notes?

Owen: What would AI predict?

Allegra: You know that’s like…it’s like 1 million years away. That’s never happening.

Owen: Look up.

[the camera pans up the the ceiling where a large and elaborate array of cables and microphones appears to be hanging, from gaff tape, from the ceiling]

Allegra: what the f*ck is that?

Owen: A…microphone. It’s a microphone array actually, but it’s built out of individual microphones.

Allegra: In the ceiling?

Owen: Yes.

Allegra: Is that HIPAA compliant?

Owen: It took about six months, but the answer is yes, that is compliant.

Allegra: You’re obsessed.

Owen: I know right? Look, the future is AI. And in the future, I don’t have to any more notes.

[Kevin, a therapist, with an attitude, enters, dressed extravagantly]

Kevin: I have a fabulous idea!

Allegra: let’s hear it.

Kevin: I am the new Chief Imagineering Officer for Brooklyn Brains!

Owen: Really?

Kevin: Ye.p

Allegra: I enjoyed the prior imagineering officer…I think his name was… Mickey Mouse.

Kevin: Wait a minute, Imagineering has been taken?

Owen: Imagineering has been the name of employees at Epcot Center since it was founded.

Kevin: (defensively) Why do you think you know everything?

Owen: My wife and I met at Epcot Center.

Kevin: you’re such a narcissist.

Allegra [attempting to diffuse the tension]: Nice shoes, where’d you get them?

Kevin: Oh, I used the corporate card!

Owen: the corporate card for this business that I own?

Kevin: My fabulousness is a legitimate business expense. Because I am in the C sweet.

Allegra: Wait a minute, Kevin. Can you spell “C suite”?

Kevin: It’s the C, and then S-w-e-e-t.

Allegra: You know what, I think you may be, the Imagineering officer we’ve been looking for.

Scene

The scene starts in darkness, and then there’s time-lapse photography of the city of New York with the sun rising. The sound of sirens is played in a montage in the background. There are no cars in the streets.

The COVID-19 virus has arrived.

—

[Calvin appears on Zoom, bundled up, in this bizarre, rustic cabin, he’s got wild hair, and wild eyes, and is wearing a strange furry cap…Owen and Allegra join the Zoom call from their office at Brooklyn Brains]

Calvin: Brandilizm

Allegra: OK, you’ve got me, what’s that?

Owen (cuts to Owen, appearing in his strange cabin, surrounded by musical instruments, recording, equipment, and cables, it’s a mess.) I also have no idea what brandalism

Calvin: it’s vandalism. Plus branding. It’s the future. Check this out.

Allegra: I’m confused

Calvin: Don’t worry, I did a lot of mushrooms last night. I am ready for this. This is my vision. Maybe you heard of my prior company? It was in Y Combinator. Yeah, you’ve heard of Y Combinator, it’s for successful entrepreneurs like myself.

Allegra: You’re very successful.

Calvin: The plant medicine gods made it clear. What we need to do, to win, is to convince JT. I hate him.

Owen: Wait a minute, you were talking about plant medicine, then JT, and then you hate him?

Calvin: He needs to accept the plant gods. It’s always about JT and his ego. He needs an ego-death, and only the plant medicine gods will do.

Allegra: Wait a minute, I’m still confused. Are you guys, like, friends? Like, you introduced us in the first place?

Calvin: Someone needs to keep him in check. He’s so greedy.

Owen: [looking a bit unsettled, then attempting to redirect]: Brandize me.

Calvin: No! Vandalized the brand—lies the brand. The brand lies. But if we vandalize it, it can tell a deeper truth.

Owen: This is what you did at Y-Combinator?

Allegra: Stranger things have come out of Y-Combinator.

Owen: Fair.

Calvin: It’s about deeper truth. Are you ready for deeper truth?

Owen: I’m ready for deep truth.

Allegra: Will it get us into Y-Combinator?

Calvin: If we vandalized the brand and reclaim it

Allegra: Then, I’m in.

End Scene

[The camera follows Carlene as she enters a run-down-looking building in East Williamsburg, Brooklyn, which is decorated like a Wild West theme inside the home].

Carly: Well, I’m home.

Owen: I mean, I thought you hadn’t left. It’s a pandemic.

Carly: Fair. What I mean is I finished my interview at Cerebellar.

Owen: You took the interview?

Carly: They have $33 million in funding from Tree Capital

Owen: Well, what happened?

Carly: The interviews went well. At least the first round. And then they had me come for a second round of Zoom interviews. I met with the founder. I don’t think the job is going to be… for me.

Owen: They have $33 million from Tree Capital.

Carly: Trust me— still not worth it.

Owen: They have $33 million from Tree. What is wrong with you? Take the gig!

Carly [Taking a deep breath]: They’re moving into…cocaine.

Owen: Wait, what?

Carly: With the pandemic, some lawyers on their team figured out that there has been a suspension of a controlled substances act. Cocaine is now, technically, legal. Nobody thinks to prescribe it. It is still a prescribable drug. And their founder wants to go big …on cocaine.

Owen: You’re kidding

Carly: I’m not kidding. I wish I was kidding. I asked some questions about how this is going to work, logistically.

Owen: Well, they must’ve had some pretty good answers, I mean, legal, had to weigh in on a plan like that?

Carly: Not exactly.

Owen: Okay, I’m waiting. Hit me.

Carly: So I’m quoting the CEO. I asked him one question and actually asked the other co-founder the same question. They both have the same answer. It was a little bit eerie, honestly.

Owen: The question wasn’t “What the f*ck is wrong with you”?

Carly: That question is not the one that I chose to ask. I asked, “What happens when the Controlled Substances Act gets reinstated?”

Owen: “…”

Carly: The answer was “We hope it doesn’t.”

Owen: From… both of them?

Carly: Word for Word.

Cut, to two weeks later.

[The phone rings, Owen picks up, Allegra is on the phone]

Allegra: hey. Did you see it?

Owen: Did I see what?

Allegra: Cerebellar just announced a new cocaine program. And HardBank funded them for another $400 million. It’s a $4.5 billion company.

Owen: Wow, Pablo Escobar missed the boat.

Allegra: I know, he just had to wait for cocaine to get a scaleable.

Owen: Well, I mean, it does have product-market fit.

Allegra: Fact.

Cut

Thanks for killing time on a Sunday with me! Stay tuned for the next thrilling installment of Reality Testing!
